chunk_map.heading: ## Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 "Sharpen the skill from evidence": line 53: "the skill (its file content carries the conventions the side-quest window *m3-quality* encoded)" and line 55: "m3-quality's authoring scrollback matters". The window name m3-security is properly introduced at line 51 with a naming parenthetical ("the main quest window (*m3-security*) now"), but m3-quality is used with a definite article as though already established, and this file never names the side-quest window at all before line 53 -- earlier chunks call it only "the side quest" (line 31, chunk 4), never the label m3-quality. That label is only assigned in the included exercise file open-the-side-quest.md (a different file), which this class resolves per-file, not cross-file, outside the named carve-outs.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the side-quest window's label at first use in this file, parallel to how m3-security is introduced, e.g. "the side-quest window (*m3-quality*)".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 "Sharpen the skill from evidence": line 55: "paste them into m3-security's chat before firing the prompt." -- "firing" (a prompt) is repo/maintainer dialect for triggering or running a prompt, explicitly named as banned by this rule's own example list, and it lands here as ordinary body prose rather than a displayed specimen.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap for plain language a student would use, e.g. "before you send the prompt" or "before you run the prompt".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering -- position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
